DISORDERS OF AMINO ACID METABOLISM
Nutrition therapy for amino acid disorders most commonly 
consists of substrate restriction, which involves limiting one 
or more essential amino acids to the minimum requirement 
while providing adequate energy and nutrients to promote 
typical growth and development (e.g., restricting phenylala-
nine [Phe] in phenylketonuria). An inadequate intake of 
an essential amino acid is often as detrimental as excess. Sup-
plementation of the product of the specific enzymatic reac-
tion usually is required in nutrition therapy for amino acid 
disorders; for example, tyrosine (Tyr) is supplemented in 
formulas for treatment of PKU.
Requirements for individual amino acids are difficult to 
determine because typical growth and development can be
